title: RTK-1 Base: Spoofed GPS Signal Detected — SM-L1

lines.msg: GPS position update received from external source via 915 MHz RF burst (10 sec). Source: 10.17.40.11 (lodge Wi-Fi). New home point set: 43.1724°N, 77.5631°W (lodge patio).
RTK-1 GPS fix lost under clear sky. Satellite count dropped from 12 to 4. No atmospheric interference detected.
915 MHz link quality spiked to 94% (normal: 70–85%). No corresponding flight activity on UAS-11 or GCS-04.
Aircraft GNSS (UAS-11) lost RTK fix simultaneously with RTK-1. Position jumped 150 meters east under clear sky. DAA-1 telemetry shows disagreement with GCS-04.
New device entry in telemetry: GCS-12 (MAC: 915-0A-1F-3C-7D-4E). Not in fleet. No record of GCS-12 in HUOG-ISP-2026.
RTK-1 and UAS-11 GNSS logs now show synchronized position jump and fix loss. Correlation confirmed.
Link integrity compromised. 915 MHz RF burst from 10.17.40.11 (lodge Wi-Fi) matches white van departure time (09:10).
All telemetry sources (RTK-1, DAA-1, GCS-04, UAS-11) now show a 150-meter eastward position jump. No visual confirmation of aircraft movement.

instructorNote: This inject confirms the GNSS spoofing and command hijack. The TL must cross-reference the RTK-1 and DAA-1 logs to validate the home point change and spoofed signal. The IC must prevent any RTL or manual override until telemetry is cleared.
